task.description: WF-03, step 1 — diagnose ISS-0103 (read the defect file first). Follow 'Step 1' of docs/workflows/WF-03-defect.md. Facts: GitHub run 41685488320 (ubuntu-24.04), test E2K-18 of tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js, the SIGTERM scenario: after the child test process was killed by SIGTERM and exited with 143, the check pidGone(pid) && groupGone(pid) was false (the log: gh run view 41685488320 --log-failed, look for not ok 105); the e2e step never ran. Green on the temporary branch run 41678354227 with the same files and many times on the Mac. FIND THE CAUSE, not the symptom, and separate three candidates with evidence: (a) a zombie: the stand-in process is dead but not yet reaped (kill(pid,0) succeeds on a zombie) because on the runner its new parent is slow to wait() — then the test must wait with a bounded poll; (b) the kit's signal hook/cleanup kills the process group asynchronously or after the child exit (a real kit defect: read tools/test/e2e/kit/cleanup.js and browser.js, the order of kill, exit and the hook; compare with the design sections on the signal hook) — then the fix is in the code and the route goes through CODE-DESIGNER; (c) the stand-in 'ok' mode ignores or delays SIGTERM/SIGKILL. Reproduce on the Mac as far as it can be (load, many repeats, an instrumented copy outside the project that logs the time between the child exit and the stand-in exit, zombie state through ps). Docker is not installed. You MAY push ONE diagnostic snapshot commit to a temporary branch ci/ISS-0103-diagnosis (built through a temporary index as in handoffs/ISS-0093-20261028-01/step-10-release-validator.json; main, the working tree and the real index unchanged; delete the branch after the run) under the owner's word recorded in decisions/0107 for temporary ci branches, with an instrumented copy of the test that prints the state (ps -o pid,ppid,stat) of the stand-in after the child exit and after each 50 ms for 3 s; a second push only if the first leaves the cause open; never push to main. Then FIND ALL PLACES OF THE SAME KIND (AP-014): every immediate pidGone/groupGone assertion in tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js and tools/test/e2e/smoke.e2e.js without a wait after a process ended (list line numbers and say for each whether it is exposed to the same race and why), and check also the runner and kit code for the same assumption. State what must change (files, one sentence each) and which of the 62 other tests would have caught or not caught it. Also say why the earlier validators' series and the GitHub branch run did not catch it. Fix nothing, commit nothing. Kill only your own processes by process id. Do not write absolute machine paths or other projects' names into project files. Report in at most 12 lines.

result.summary: Cause: the test asserts a state that the kernel has not reached yet. After the child test process ends, E2K-18 checks pidGone(pid) && groupGone(pid) once (e2e-kit.test.js:1070-1071). The kit kills the stand-in with SIGKILL in cleanupAllSync (cleanup.js:205, run from exitNow:261-269 and from the process 'exit' handler:314) and then ends the process; signal delivery and the reaping of the dead stand-in are asynchronous, and kill(pid,0) / kill(-pgid,0) also succeed on a zombie that its new parent (init/the runner's systemd) has not reaped yet. So the assertion races with the death/reaping of the stand-in; on a loaded 2-4 core runner the window is long enough. Candidates: (a) CONFIRMED in kind (zombie / not yet dead = the same asynchronous window): a node parent that SIGKILLs a group and does not reap leaves a process that ps shows as Z and for which both kill checks succeed (self_check Z1); on the Mac under 12 busy loops the exact E2K-18 SIGTERM scenario was red on the immediate check in 3 of 160 runs, and the stand-in was gone 8.5-10.5 ms later (P2, P3). (b) REFUTED as a kit defect: the order is right (hooks list empty for the child -> exitNow -> SIGKILL to the group is sent BEFORE process.exit; the registry is cleared, nothing is killed twice); the kit cannot wait in a sync 'exit' handler, and everything the kit awaits in the same process (close, abortStart, stopGroup) polls kill(-pgid,0) with timers (cleanup.js:66-73), which also lets libuv reap. The design F20 says 'SIGKILL of the group is instant': true for the call, not for the death; this sentence and the E2K-18 row 'the stand-in pid is gone' (design 11.3) assume an instant effect and are the root of the missing wait. (c) REFUTED: the 'ok' stand-in does not touch signals (only 'ok-ignore-term' ignores SIGTERM, fake-chrome.js:~55), the signal of the test goes to the child test process, not to the stand-in, and the stand-in is ended by SIGKILL, which cannot be ignored. NOT CONFIRMED: on Linux itself whether the stand-in was a zombie or still running at the check (Docker is absent, no ps state from the runner, the diagnostic CI push was not made: both states are removed by the same fix; one push can settle it if the owner wants the fact). Why the tests did not catch it: no test waits after a process end that was caused by an asynchronous kill; the series of the validators (5-6 runs of npm run e2e, test runs) and the author's runs were all on macOS where launchd reaps in about 2 ms and the window is ~0 (3 of 160 even under load); the branch run 41678354227 was one sample on ubuntu. This is a defect of the test (Q5), not of the kit code. What must change: see issues I4. Severity MEDIUM (no earlier defect with this cause).
result.self_check:
Environment: macOS, Node v22.23.4, fresh clone of the tag base/ISS-0103-20261103-01 (HEAD 30ab39c) in the scratchpad; nothing in the project changed except this handoff; one command at a time; my burner processes were killed by pid.

L0. CI log: gh run view 41685488320 --log-failed -> 'not ok 105 - E2K-18 ...', duration_ms 177.86, error 'SIGTERM: the stand-in is gone', e2e-kit.test.js:1070:16; E2K-19 passes next; the job has 8 steps, 'Run the check' failed, runs-on ubuntu-24.04. The failed scenario is the FIRST one (SIGTERM).

Z1. A zombie passes both checks (scratch script: spawn detached `sleep 30`, process.kill(-pid,'SIGKILL'), busy loop 300 ms in the parent, no reaping):
$ node zombie.mjs
kill(pid,0) succeeds: true  kill(-pgid,0) succeeds: true
  PID  PPID STAT
34292 34285 Z

P1. Probe = the E2K-18 scenario outside the project (same start.mjs, same stand-in, same SIGTERM; after the child 'close' it checks pidGone && groupGone once, then polls every 1 ms and prints the time until gone). Quiet Mac:
$ node test/probe.mjs SIGTERM 20
... 20 lines 'code=143 immediate=true ... goneAfterMs=1.7-2.1'
immediate failures: 0/20

P2. Under 12 busy loops (nice 10), SIGTERM, 30 runs x 3:
16 code=143 immediate=false firstStat="none" goneAfterMs=8.9
immediate failures: 1/30
16 code=143 immediate=false firstStat="none" goneAfterMs=8.5
immediate failures: 1/30
immediate failures: 0/30   (max goneAfterMs 12.7 / 14.6 / 11.2)

P3. Second series, 12 busy loops, 40 runs x 4: 'immediate=false ... goneAfterMs=10.5', immediate failures 1/40, 0/40, 0/40, 0/40. (The state in 'firstStat' is 'none' because the ps process itself takes about 10 ms, longer than the window: the zombie-or-running split on Linux is not measured.)

T1. The real tests on the Mac under the same load (node --test --test-name-pattern, 40 runs each): E2K-18 0/40 red, E2K-38 0/40 red. So the window is hit by the probe (a tight check right at 'close') but not by the test on the Mac in 80 runs: the test cannot be shown red on this machine, which is why a deterministic regression test is needed (I5).

Code reading: cleanup.js:205 signalGroup SIGKILL, no wait; cleanup.js:261-269 exitNow; cleanup.js:314 process.on('exit'); cleanup.js:66-73 waitGroupGone polls kill(-pgid,0) every 20 ms; browser.js:150-160 abortStart and :112 close wait through it; runner.js:207 and :253 sweepBrowserRegistry SIGKILL without wait; fake-chrome.js with-child: the child is in the same group (no detached).

issues.text: No closed defect has this cause (grep of docs/issues, anti-patterns, decisions for zombie/pidGone/groupGone/ESRCH/reap: only ISS-0103 itself). Other flaky-test defects are other causes (ISS-0075 readdir/lstat, ISS-0015 snapshot, ISS-0017 background processes, ISS-0083 parallel load). Not a return of an earlier cause; severity proposal: MEDIUM (stays): the check on main is red, a flaky test (decisions/0079 p.2), no product behaviour is wrong.

PLACES OF THE SAME KIND, tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js, immediate pidGone/groupGone after a process ended. EXPOSED (the last kill is a SIGKILL without a wait, in a process that then exits, and the test checks at once after the exit of that process): (1) lines 1070-1071, E2K-18, all five scenarios SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP/exit/throw (same exit path cleanupAllSync; reproduced for SIGTERM, the other four share the code). (2) lines 2825-2831, E2K-38 (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP to the runner while a spec runs): leader, spec, browser, stand-in pids after run.done; the browser has its own group and is ended by the spec's exitNow or by the runner hook's sweepBrowserRegistry (runner.js:207), both SIGKILL without wait, then the runner exits. (3) line 2869, E2K-38 preflight part (signal during the preflight): logPids(log) pidGone && groupGone after run.done; the stand-in is ended by the runner's cleanupAllSync. NOT EXPOSED (a bounded wait precedes the check): 701 (failedStart: abortStart waits for the group, cleanup.js/browser.js:~150), 747 (START_TIMEOUT, same), 731 (START_EXITED: the stand-in ended itself and node has reaped it before 'exit' is emitted), 805 (browser.close() waits for the group), 988-989 and 1005 (after await close(): stopGroup polls the whole group, the child of with-child is in the same group), 2233, 2939, 3261, 3342, 3441 (use until), 3266 (after until on every pid), 3459 (stoppedPids are all waited at 3342 before). 2986: the spec ended by itself, nothing was killed, not of the kind. Checks of the opposite direction (986, 3414, 3419: !pidGone, a process must be alive) cannot fail from lateness. test/e2e/smoke.e2e.js:142,166,188,227,388 assertCleaned: processGone + groupGone once, but always after withBrowser, whose close() has already waited for the group by polling: not exposed. Outside the named scope, for ORCH: test/exec-helpers.js pidAlive/groupAliveOf are used with waitUntil (a bounded poll, the model to copy); assertDead in test/exec-closure.test.js:121 and test/team-helpers.js:853 is immediate, but its callers (exec-closure 374, 462, 512; team-helpers 869; team-recovery 1616) check a child that spawnSync has already waited for: not of the kind.

KIT AND RUNNER CODE with the same assumption 'SIGKILL has taken effect': cleanup.js:205 cleanupAllSync, cleanup.js:161 sweepBrowserRegistry (called at runner.js:207 hook, :253 after each spec, :335 dropBrowserRegistry, cleanup.js:188 cleanupAllSync). In production nothing reads the result at once, and the profile folder is removed with retries (cleanup.js:83-90), so no kit defect; the kit is not to be changed. Waiting places that are right: waitGroupGone, stopGroup, abortStart, close. The rule 'a gone pid may be reused' (cleanup.js:184) is kept: the registry is cleared before the kill.

WHAT MUST CHANGE (behaviour, not code), WF-03 step 3. (1) tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js: in the three exposed places (1070, 2825-2831, 2869) the check 'pid and group are gone' becomes a bounded wait: poll every 20 ms, up to a stated limit (5 s as the file already uses for the same kind at 3261), failing with a message that names the pid and its state; one helper used by all three, and by neither a longer fixed sleep nor a weaker assertion (Q6); the file already has `until` (line 124), so the helper is a thin 'pidAndGroupGone(pid)' over it, taken once instead of repeating pidGone && groupGone. Because a zombie also passes kill(0), the helper must still end only when ESRCH is seen: it must not accept 'alive' after the limit. (2) docs/design/REQ-104-e2e-chrome-kit.md: state that SIGKILL takes effect after the call returns and a test waits (the fact F20 'SIGKILL of the group is instant' and the E2K-18 / E2K-38 rows of 11.3 say 'is gone' without a wait). (3) decisions/0108-e2e-kit-conventions.md: add the convention 'after a kill, a test waits with a limit for ESRCH; no single kill(pid,0) after a process end' (an addendum; CODE-DESIGNER decides the place). (4) No change in the kit code (cleanup.js, browser.js, runner.js) and none in the stand-in. Expected behaviour exists: criterion 3/11 of REQ-104 and E2K-18/E2K-38 already require 'the stand-in is gone'; no WF-01 step is needed.

FOR TEST-DESIGNER (step 6). The race cannot be hit on the Mac by the real E2K-18 (0/80 red under load, T1), so the regression test pins the helper and the three places by a deterministic state: a zombie. Reproduction before the fix: scratch script Z1 (spawn a detached stand-in or `sleep`, SIGKILL its group, keep the parent's event loop blocked for ~300 ms, then run the single check pidGone(pid) && groupGone(pid)) gives false while ps shows STAT Z (output in self_check). The new test: a fixture parent that kills a stand-in group and blocks its loop for a stated time before it exits; the test then runs the new wait on the pid and requires it to return true after the block ends and to report a bounded failure message if the process stays (a stand-in that ignores SIGKILL cannot exist, so the failure branch uses a live process). The old single check on the same fixture must be shown red on the pre-fix copy (fresh clone of the tag): that is the 'fails before the fix' proof. Mutants for TEST-DESIGNER: the helper does a single check (no loop), the loop ends at the limit with true, the limit is ignored. The probe script of this diagnosis (test/probe.mjs, in the scratch clone only) shows the real-scenario rates for a series: 3 of 160 under load.

WHICH OF THE 62 OTHER TESTS WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: none. E2K-38 (same exposure) passed in the same CI run only by timing; the tests with `until` are immune and are not a detector; E2K-17, E2K-39 and the smoke tests wait on the group before the check. There is no test that holds a stand-in's death or reaping late. Why the series did not catch it: all validator series and runs were on macOS (launchd reaps within about 2 ms; 3 of 160 even under 12 busy loops), the runs on GitHub were two (one green on the temporary branch 41678354227, one red on main): a 1-in-N race at the default load of a 4-core runner needs about 20+ runs to show; the quality-bar series rule for flaky tests (20 full runs, 100 file runs, normal and under load) applies to the new fix: run it on the Mac under load and, if the owner agrees, as a series on a temporary ci branch under decisions/0107.

Q13, an entry for docs/anti-patterns.md: 'A test checked that a killed process is gone with one kill(pid,0) right after the parent ended; a SIGKILL is delivered and reaped after the call returns, and a zombie still answers kill(pid,0), so the test was right on the machine of the author and red on the runner. The design recorded "SIGKILL is instant" as a fact from a sketch on one machine.' Rule: after any kill the test waits with a limit for ESRCH (a loop), on the machine of the author the window is nearly zero and proves nothing about the runner; a fact about timing is taken in more than one state (AP-100). Related: AP-012 (the sketch fact F20 was not checked for the other platform).

WHAT I DID NOT DO. (a) The instrumented CI snapshot (ci/ISS-0103-diagnosis) was not pushed: nothing about zombie versus not-yet-dead on Linux is measured, and I did not spend a CI cycle on a fact that does not change the fix; if the owner wants it, one push of the probe with `ps -o pid,ppid,stat` sampled every 50 ms for 3 s after the child exit settles it. (b) No Docker. (c) No real Chrome was started; only the stand-in. (d) The runner's tests E2K-38 were run by name only (40 times); E2K-33/E2K-37 and the others were not re-run. No new defect found on the way.
